messages.content: My coach said the match was "called off". Will it happen later?

Probably not. "Call off" means to cancel something that was planned. If the match will happen later, people usually say it was "postponed".
Example: The match was called off because the ground was flooded.
Find out: does it mean the same as discover?

Mostly, yes. "Find out" means to learn a fact or a piece of information, often by asking or checking. It is more common than "discover" in everyday speech.
Example: Shreya called the office to find out when the results would be announced.
Can "get over" be used for feelings?

Yes. "Get over" means to feel better after something unpleasant, like an illness, a shock or a sad event.
Example: It took Noor a few weeks to get over the loss of her pet cat.
How do you spell the word for a person you work with: colleage or colleague?

The correct spelling is "colleague", ending in -gue, like "league". Both words have the same "eague" pattern.
Example: My colleague Wei helped me fix the spreadsheet.
Buisness or business? I can never remember.

The correct spelling is "business". Think of it as "busy" plus "ness": the y changes to i, giving bus-i-ness.
Example: Harpreet's uncle runs a small business selling handmade candles.
Formally or formerly: which should I pick for "my ___ school"?

Neither fits exactly. "Former" is the adjective that means earlier, so say "my former school". "Formerly" is an adverb meaning in the past, and "formally" means in a formal or official way.
Examples: She was formerly a teacher. The prize was formally announced today.
His name "rings a bell", but I can't remember where from. What does that mean?

If a name or fact rings a bell, it sounds familiar and reminds you of something you have heard before.
Example: Her name rings a bell, but I cannot remember where we met.
Our manager said a new project is "in the pipeline". Where is the pipeline?

There is no real pipeline. If something is in the pipeline, it is being planned or prepared and will happen soon.
Example: A new library is in the pipeline for our town.
My brother says filling in the form twice is "a pain in the neck". Does his neck hurt?

No. A pain in the neck is an informal way to say that something, or someone, is very annoying.
Example: Standing in two queues for one ticket is a pain in the neck.
Is it "pasttime" or "pastime"?

The correct spelling is "pastime", with only one t in the middle: pas-time.
Example: Reading is her favourite pastime.
When I wanted to ask about the old quarrel, my mother said "let sleeping dogs lie". Why?

It means do not stir up an old problem that is quiet now, because you may cause more trouble.
Example: The two neighbours have not argued for years, so let sleeping dogs lie.
Our teacher said that Nina and Pooja are "birds of a feather". Are they both birdwatchers?

Not necessarily. The full saying is "birds of a feather flock together", and it means that people with similar interests or characters tend to become friends.
Example: Both of them love chess and old films, so they are birds of a feather.
When do I write "anyone" and when "any one"?

Write "anyone" when you mean any person. Write "any one" as two words when you mean a single one from a group.
Examples: Is anyone at home? You may choose any one of these books.
I got a call from an unknown person who asked for someone else. How can I say politely that they have the wrong number?

You can say, "I think you have the wrong number." Or say, "I'm sorry, there is no one here by that name." Both are polite.
Example: I'm sorry, I think you have the wrong number.
Parents can "opt out" of the school trip. What does that mean?

"Opt out" means to choose not to take part in something.
Example: You can opt out of the email list at any time.
Is it a "rucksack" or a "backpack"?

Both words describe a bag carried on the back. "Rucksack" is common in British English, while "backpack" is American and also widely used in India.
Examples: She packed her rucksack for the trek. She packed her backpack for the trek.
The librarian helped me "track down" an old book. Did she follow footprints?

No. "Track down" means to find something or someone after a careful search.
Example: After a long search, we tracked down the owner of the lost bag.
When should I use brackets like ( ) in a sentence?

Round brackets, also called parentheses, hold extra information that could be removed without breaking the sentence.
Example: My cousin (who lives in Pune) is visiting us this week.
The notice says "sorry for the inconvenience". Who is saying sorry for what?

The people who wrote the notice are apologising because something, such as a delay or a change, causes trouble for readers.
Example: Sorry for the inconvenience; the library will be closed on Monday.
Do I put the title of a short poem in quotation marks?

Yes. Titles of short works such as poems, short stories and articles usually go in quotation marks. Titles of whole books are usually written in italics or underlined instead.
Example: We learned the poem "The Road Not Taken" in class.
